LESSON: WRITING5.5.1 LETTER OF APPLICATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.5: Writing5.5.1 Letter of Application
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing5.5.1 Letter of Application, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we write letters of application? 2. How can one ensure a letter of application meets the expected standards?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing5.5.1 Letter of Application together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration : Learner develop teamwork skills as he/she participates in collaborative letter writing tasks

• Digital literacy: Learner interact with technology skills as he/she searchers for samples of letters of application from the internet

• Creativity and imagination: Learner composes a letter of application for placement at Senior Secondary School which boosts

their level of innovativeness

Values:
● Unity: is promoted as the learner exchanges the letter of application with others for peer assessment

● Responsibility: is fostered as groups of learners participate in collaborative letter writing and editing
